listing.name: Political Map - Sector Map Layers
listing.summary: Currently in pre-release. Requires LazyLib and LunaLib. Safe to enable mid-save, uninstalled via settings.
listing.aiSummary: Adds a political map overlay to the sector map, intel screen, and minimap that visualizes faction presence, claims, and domination.

description:
Political Map

as the headline feature of

Sector Map Layers

This is the pre-release stage intended for public testing and feedback collection.
You can try this mod early and share your experiences, so I can improve it.

Are you struggling to

keep track of faction presence and growth

?

Do you want to know

which systems are claimed and by who

before you even take the trip there?

Do you want to

paint the map

with your conquests?

Do you just want to

see all that border gore

factions in your mod list produce?

Do you want to

play Bad Apple

?

This mod requires

LazyLib

,

LunaLib

.

It's

safe to install mid-run

,

and there's a short

uninstall procedure

you will need to follow if you decide to keep your save after uninstalling the mod.

This mod is made compatible with

Nexerelin

,

Fast Rendering

,

Random Assortment of Things

.

Sector Map Layers

is an overlay for the map screen

(Tab, Q)

, the intel screen

(E, 1)

, the minimap in the bottom right corner of the screen (replaces the vanilla radar) if you have

Random Assortment of Things

installed.

Examples

Map screen.

Intel screen.

Random Assortment of Things

minimap.

[close]

Everything is calculated and drawn off of game data, and it gets updated as the state of the sector shanges. Map layers don't alter any of the data being used to draw it, making map layers

read-only

by design.

[close]How to access map layers

KMU

comes with

Sector Map Layers

feature turned on by default. After loading a save or starting a new game, when you open the

map screen

or the

intel screen

, you'll see a new

Map layers

button among map filter buttons. Clicking that button or pressing

(M)

enables the map layer overlay and its sidebar.

Map screen.

Intel screen.

[close]

The main control interface of map layers is the collapsible

sidebar

that lists all available layers and related knobs and toggles.

Available map layersPolitical Map (P)

Focuses on populated colonies (markets) and their affiliation.
Only they paint the map.Decivilised markets are treated as populated and aligned with Neutral faction (politically disorganised as contrasted by the Independent faction). Systems only with decivilised markets are painted in their own style (adjustable in settings).Markets with Abandoned Station condition are treated as unpopulated and produce no map paint.All non-market entities produce no map paint.
Examples
Unclaimed unpopulated systems are drawn very faintly just to show where systems touch.
Those outlines of unpopulated systems can be toggled on and off independently from populated systems,
which are always drawn even when there's no organised faction in the system (e.g. all colonies in a system are decivilised).
You can also adjust their visual style independently from faction and decivilised systems.
[close]Any given system can be painted by only a single faction, so each system draws a presence ribbon hugging its border that represents each populated colony with the color of the faction holding them. Ribbons are shortened to represent solidified control when only a single faction or alliance is present is a system, while that presence is in no violation of unconditional claims.

Examples
Presence ribbons: Samarra draws one showing 3 Hegemony markets and 1 Independent market.
[close]Expandable system tooltips provide detailed information on how each market affects the balance of power.

Examples
Tooltips list Neutral (unowned) markets.

Tooltips list markets producing no domination score.
[close]Factions holding any population centers are listed in a sortable filter. Selecting any of them spotlights their presence across the sector. Neutral is listed there alongside organised factions, so selecting it spotlights every system holding decivilised colonies.
In domination views (Factions and Alliances) solid fill represents domination, hatched fill represents presence in a system dominated by somebody else, no fill represents claims on unpopulated systems.On the Claims view all systems are painted with solid fill.
Examples
Faction filter, expanded to 2 columns, sorted by faction attitude toward the player.

Factions view filtered by Luddic Church.

Factions view filtered by Pirates.

Unpopulated systems get no paint in domination views.
Tia star system is shown as Hegemony-owned because Hegemony holds an unconditional claim for it.
[close]

The

Political Map

comes with 3 views:

Factions - paints faction territory based on a custom domination algorithm (highly customisable in settings) that weighs markets sizes, stability, whether a market is hidden, presence of an orbital station (or if a station is militarised), and the number of patrol fleets generated (by their sizes).

Examples
Luddic Church unconditionally claims Penelope's Star but isn't present there,
and per domination rules actually present faction (Independent) reads as the holder.
The claim is still listed in the tooltip.
[close]Alliances (only visible with Nexerelin installed) - same as Factions but allied factions stand as a single political entity with their holdings combined.

Examples
Tooltips in the Alliances view combine domination score of present alliance members.
[close]Claims - paints faction territory based on the vanilla system claim mechanic - dynamic or unconditional. Unconditional claims are set via sector memory and are the highest authority. Unless a claim is unconditional, system claim is resolved dynamically - the single biggest market (that participates in the economy) wins, boosted by the presence of same-faction markets (of any kind) and any military industry constructed. The player faction and non-territorial factions cannot lay claims dynamically. If you filter by a non-territorial faction, unclaimed systems with their presence will be spotlit.

Examples
Luddic Church isn't present in Penelope's Star system, holds an unconditional claim on it,
and there's a non-territorial faction (Independent) present.
[close]

[close][close]Spoiler protectionTo avoid spoilers, map layers operate on a vanilla-derived

visibility

system

(each component is available in settings)

:

Hidden systems (with no hyperspace anchor generated off of a star, nebula, or a black hole) are not revealed unless there's a visible population center present or it holds an active gate.Entities marked as discoverable (hidden on the system map until in range of player fleet sensors) are not revealed. They are also listed on Claims tooltips because vanilla uses them in claim calculations, but are redacted.Markets marked as hidden are not revealed if there are no visible colonies held by other non-allied factions, or until the player visits their system. They are also listed on Claims tooltips because vanilla uses them in claim calculations, but are redacted.Decivilised markets are not revealed unless they start so, or until the player visits their system.Unowned markets with the Abandoned Station condition follow visibility rules of hidden markets.

[close]

This mod comes with a suite of

LunaLib

settings that allow you to tweak, visuals, sound volume, keybinds, underlying mechanics.

descriptionHtml:
Political Map
as the headline feature of Sector Map Layers

This is the pre-release stage intended for public testing and feedback collection.
You can try this mod early and share your experiences, so I can improve it.
Are you struggling to keep track of faction presence and growth?
Do you want to know which systems are claimed and by who before you even take the trip there?
Do you want to paint the map with your conquests?
Do you just want to see all that border gore factions in your mod list produce?
Do you want to play Bad Apple?


This mod requires LazyLib, LunaLib.
It's safe to install mid-run,
and there's a short uninstall procedure you will need to follow if you decide to keep your save after uninstalling the mod.
This mod is made compatible with Nexerelin, Fast Rendering, Random Assortment of Things.
Sector Map Layers is an overlay for the map screen (Tab, Q), the intel screen (E, 1), the minimap in the bottom right corner of the screen (replaces the vanilla radar) if you have Random Assortment of Things installed.

Examples
Map screen.

Intel screen.

Random Assortment of Things minimap.
[close]
Everything is calculated and drawn off of game data, and it gets updated as the state of the sector shanges. Map layers don't alter any of the data being used to draw it, making map layers read-only by design.

Sector examples
Vanilla.

Lightly modded.

Heavily modded.
[close]How to access map layersKMU comes with Sector Map Layers feature turned on by default. After loading a save or starting a new game, when you open the map screen or the intel screen, you'll see a new Map layers button among map filter buttons. Clicking that button or pressing (M) enables the map layer overlay and its sidebar.

Map screen.

Intel screen.
[close]
The main control interface of map layers is the collapsible sidebar that lists all available layers and related knobs and toggles.

Available map layersPolitical Map (P)
  • Focuses on populated colonies (markets) and their affiliation.
    • Only they paint the map.
    • Decivilised markets are treated as populated and aligned with Neutral faction (politically disorganised as contrasted by the Independent faction). Systems only with decivilised markets are painted in their own style (adjustable in settings).
    • Markets with Abandoned Station condition are treated as unpopulated and produce no map paint.
    • All non-market entities produce no map paint.

    Examples
    Unclaimed unpopulated systems are drawn very faintly just to show where systems touch.
    Those outlines of unpopulated systems can be toggled on and off independently from populated systems,
    which are always drawn even when there's no organised faction in the system (e.g. all colonies in a system are decivilised).
    You can also adjust their visual style independently from faction and decivilised systems.
    [close]
  • Any given system can be painted by only a single faction, so each system draws a presence ribbon hugging its border that represents each populated colony with the color of the faction holding them. Ribbons are shortened to represent solidified control when only a single faction or alliance is present is a system, while that presence is in no violation of unconditional claims.

    Examples
    Presence ribbons: Samarra draws one showing 3 Hegemony markets and 1 Independent market.
    [close]
  • Expandable system tooltips provide detailed information on how each market affects the balance of power.

    Examples
    Tooltips list Neutral (unowned) markets.

    Tooltips list markets producing no domination score.
    [close]
  • Factions holding any population centers are listed in a sortable filter. Selecting any of them spotlights their presence across the sector. Neutral is listed there alongside organised factions, so selecting it spotlights every system holding decivilised colonies.
    • In domination views (Factions and Alliances) solid fill represents domination, hatched fill represents presence in a system dominated by somebody else, no fill represents claims on unpopulated systems.
    • On the Claims view all systems are painted with solid fill.

    Examples
    Faction filter, expanded to 2 columns, sorted by faction attitude toward the player.

    Factions view filtered by Luddic Church.

    Factions view filtered by Pirates.

    Unpopulated systems get no paint in domination views.
    Tia star system is shown as Hegemony-owned because Hegemony holds an unconditional claim for it.
    [close]

The Political Map comes with 3 views:
  • Factions - paints faction territory based on a custom domination algorithm (highly customisable in settings) that weighs markets sizes, stability, whether a market is hidden, presence of an orbital station (or if a station is militarised), and the number of patrol fleets generated (by their sizes).

    Examples
    Luddic Church unconditionally claims Penelope's Star but isn't present there,
    and per domination rules actually present faction (Independent) reads as the holder.
    The claim is still listed in the tooltip.
    [close]
  • Alliances (only visible with Nexerelin installed) - same as Factions but allied factions stand as a single political entity with their holdings combined.

    Examples
    Tooltips in the Alliances view combine domination score of present alliance members.
    [close]
  • Claims - paints faction territory based on the vanilla system claim mechanic - dynamic or unconditional. Unconditional claims are set via sector memory and are the highest authority. Unless a claim is unconditional, system claim is resolved dynamically - the single biggest market (that participates in the economy) wins, boosted by the presence of same-faction markets (of any kind) and any military industry constructed. The player faction and non-territorial factions cannot lay claims dynamically. If you filter by a non-territorial faction, unclaimed systems with their presence will be spotlit.

    Examples
    Luddic Church isn't present in Penelope's Star system, holds an unconditional claim on it,
    and there's a non-territorial faction (Independent) present.
    [close]
[close][close]Spoiler protectionTo avoid spoilers, map layers operate on a vanilla-derived visibility system (each component is available in settings):
  • Hidden systems (with no hyperspace anchor generated off of a star, nebula, or a black hole) are not revealed unless there's a visible population center present or it holds an active gate.
  • Entities marked as discoverable (hidden on the system map until in range of player fleet sensors) are not revealed. They are also listed on Claims tooltips because vanilla uses them in claim calculations, but are redacted.
  • Markets marked as hidden are not revealed if there are no visible colonies held by other non-allied factions, or until the player visits their system. They are also listed on Claims tooltips because vanilla uses them in claim calculations, but are redacted.
  • Decivilised markets are not revealed unless they start so, or until the player visits their system.
  • Unowned markets with the Abandoned Station condition follow visibility rules of hidden markets.
[close]
This mod comes with a suite of LunaLib settings that allow you to tweak, visuals, sound volume, keybinds, underlying mechanics.

Console commandsIf you've got Console Commands installed you can make use of the following commands.

Provided by KMU:
  • kmu_profiling [tree|flat|walks] [namespace=<prefix>] [top=<count>] [perframe] [reset] - Writes full or scoped performance measurements to game logs on demand. Calls exceeding the budget are logged automatically without this command. Requires profiling to be enabled in settings.

Provided by KMLib:
  • kmlib_activate_gate <id> - Activates the gate with that id in the current system.
  • kmlib_colonise [entity-id] [faction-id] - Founds a colony. [entity-id] defaults to the nearest[fa

aiDescription: Introduces a read-only map layer system that paints the sector based on faction control, using a custom domination algorithm that weighs market size, stability, and military presence. Includes three distinct views: Factions, Alliances (with Nexerelin), and Claims, each with detailed tooltips and filtering options. Features a spoiler protection system that respects vanilla visibility rules for hidden systems and markets.
